subject: Relaxing the exclusion restriction in Stan.

messages.author: c7f51a5f77294074
messages.subject: Relaxing the exclusion restriction in Stan.
parts:
Hi all,
I wrote a model that takes into account possible violations of the exclusion restriction. I've tested it on randomly generated data and it works really well if you guess how much the exclusion restriction is violated. Any input is welcome.

I tried an earlier model without modeling the correlation between the causal effect of interest and how much the exclusion restriction is violated and that worked ok, but on large amounts of actual data the model just spit out zeros for the mean and sd of the parameters b and l. This was built from this post here.

data {
   int<lower=0> n;
   matrix[n,2] yt; //first and second stages
   vector[n] z; //instrument
}

parameters {
   real b;
   real d;
   real a;
   real g;
   real l;
   real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_t;
   real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_y;
   real<lower=-1,upper=1> rho_yt;
   real<lower=-1,upper=1> exclude_correlation; //correlation between causal effect and violation of exclusion restriction
}

transformed parameters {
   cov_matrix[2] Sigma_yt;
   matrix[n,2] yt_hat;
   matrix[2,2] L;
   cov_matrix[2] exclude_cor_matrix;
   vector[2] exclude_param_vector;
   vector[2] exclude_mean_vector;

   Sigma_yt[1,1] <- pow(sigma_y,2);
   Sigma_yt[2,2] <- pow(sigma_t,2);
   Sigma_yt[1,2] <- rho_yt*sigma_y*sigma_t;
   Sigma_yt[2,1] <- Sigma_yt[1,2];

   exclude_cor_matrix[1,1]<-1;
   exclude_cor_matrix[2,2]<-1;
   exclude_cor_matrix[1,2]<-exclude_correlation;
   exclude_cor_matrix[2,1]<-exclude_cor_matrix[1,2];

   exclude_param_vector[1]<-l; //this is how much the instrument violates the exclusion restriction
   exclude_param_vector[2]<-b; //this is the causal effect I am trying to identify

   exclude_mean_vector[1]<-0;
   exclude_mean_vector[2]<-0;

   for (i in 1:n) {
      yt_hat[i,2] <- g + d*z[i];
      yt_hat[i,1] <- a + b*yt_hat[i,2]+l*z[i];
   }

   L <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma_yt);
}

model{
   sigma_y ~ cauchy(0,1);
   sigma_t ~ cauchy(0,1);
   rho_yt ~ uniform(-1,1);
   exclude_correlation ~ normal(0,.1); //this seems helps identify the parameters l and b
   l ~ normal (0,1); //this is my prior on how much the exclusion restriction should be relaxed
   d ~ normal (0,1);
   a ~ normal (0,1);
   g ~ normal (0,1);
   L ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(1);

   exclude_param_vector~multi_normal(exclude_mean_vector,exclude_cor_matrix);

   for (i in 1:n)
     transpose(yt[i]) ~ multi_normal_cholesky(transpose(yt_hat[i]), L);
}


I've attached an example with randomly generated data in R.

-Rick

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Relaxing the exclusion restriction in Stan.
parts:
Hi, without looking at the model in detail, let me just say that when we fit latent variable models, we typically want to assign informative priors for the variance parameters. This <lower=0,upper=100> thing is a bad idea. What you want to do is set <lower=0> and then use an informative prior to keep the variance parameter to a reasonable value. Also, no need to decompose the cov matrix into rho, etc. That’s Bugs-style coding. With Stan I think it’s best to just work with the cov matrix or its Cholesky factor all at once.
A
